project.name: Apple TV per-app Denon volume
project.summary: Production accepted and project closed by the user on September 6, 2026. App switches now start changing volume in about 2 seconds, compared with the measured 5.6-second baseline. Home 50 and Netflix 61 restore correctly with the refreshed WebUI open, including on the original separate USB power adapter. Screensaver retains the app volume. Firmware c72b48ec and collector 36dc7c21 are deployed; no further flash, Home Assistant change or restart is required. Release commit: 0d06c30. Historical acceptance and explicitly untested cases remain below.

tasks.name: Sep 6 · Latency and WebUI release
done: Measured the baseline Home 50.0 to Netflix 61.0 switch at 5.60 seconds to first observed movement
Split the baseline into 3.55 seconds to MQTT recovery, 1.60 seconds to ESP restoration and 0.46 seconds to observed movement
Confirmed the user's 5 to 6 second observation; the earlier general report of 10 to 15 seconds was not reproduced
Preserved the full 3 second wake, screensaver and transport guard while shortening only brief ambiguity
Passed independent review, all 31 collector tests and all 51 focused Home Assistant tests
Backed up and deployed collector SHA 36dc7c21 with PID 4173979, zero restarts and no HA or ESP firmware change
Passed the first normal post-deploy switch at about 2 seconds before motion, exact raw 122, idle, no error and no overshoot
Live-proved the shortened ambiguity branch: offline at 06:23:21.096 UTC to Netflix at 21.575 took 0.479 seconds versus the 3.55 second baseline
With unchanged firmware under Mac USB power, completed a phone-WebUI-open Netflix switch at the physically confirmed 61.0 target without panic, watchdog reset or network loss
Completed a private 4 MB flash backup and verified the prior live app image matched the accepted HEAD lineage
Flashed firmware c72b48ec application-only at offset 0x10000 and 115200 baud with esptool data-hash verification
Passed initial post-flash readback: Wi-Fi and Bluetooth reconnected, state connected, idle and error-free at raw 122, with all eight app rows preserved
Passed refreshed-phone-UI-open Home to Netflix and Netflix to Home switches at about 2 seconds each, reaching exact 61.0 and 50.0
Confirmed Home saved raw 100, display 50.0, with the ESP connected, idle and error-free and all other seven rows unchanged
Measured event-to-first-motion at 1.17 and 1.15 seconds with about 0.1 second clock uncertainty while retaining the 750 ms one-DVT-sample debounce
Passed screensaver retention: the receiver kept the last app volume and returning to the same app caused no redundant volume change
Passed Home and Netflix switching with the phone Web UI open on the original separate power adapter; the user accepted production behavior
Closed the accepted release at commit 0d06c30 with no further Home Assistant change or restart
User accepted screensaver entry and dismissal retaining Netflix volume 61
User confirmed production operation on the original separate USB power adapter after the UI-open switching check
Aligned MQTT and UART clocks showed about 1.17 seconds and 1.15 seconds from foreground event to first reported movement; estimated clock uncertainty about 0.1 second
Retained the 750 ms app debounce to allow a following DVT sample to correct a transient identity; no absolute minimum latency claim
Final release checks passed: 43 Home Assistant tests, 31 collector tests, controller and WebUI regressions, firmware build and privacy scan
Closed the accepted scope at the user request; no further Home Assistant changes or firmware flashing needed

Passed initial pairing, volume up and down, ESP restart recovery and receiver power-cycle recovery
Added fixed LAN configuration, mDNS, captive setup access and the local HTTP API
Added the local responsive web UI for connection, pairing, receiver state and half-step volume control

tasks.name: Sep 1 to 2 · Exact and fast volume control
done: Built one shared setVolume path with target identity, replacement detection and HTTP 409 conflict protection

tasks.name: Sep 2 to 6 · Project visibility and verification
done: Added the local live status dashboard and persistent loopback-only server

tasks.name: Documented limits outside the closed release
done: The earlier intermittent network disappearance was not assigned a root cause; the accepted safeguards and original-adapter production rerun passed
Rapid transient switching and deliberate multi-client stress were not separately exercised before user acceptance
Broader DVT fault injection, active-target link loss and full power-cycle matrix rows remain historical deferred coverage rather than release blockers
pending: The original intermittent network disappearance was reproduced, but its precise cause remains unproven. The bounded UI polling fix passed subsequent USB and original-adapter production checks.
Deliberate rapid transient-app and multiple simultaneous WebUI-client stress tests were not performed.

Broader DVT fault injection, active-target or temporary-unmute link loss, all-app power-cycle persistence, and remaining sentinel/manual-intervention cases retain their historical unaccepted status. No changes for these cases are included in this release.

nodes.detail: Foreground lifecycle and DVT state identify the current app without requiring playback.
nodes.evidence: Home, Netflix, YouTube and Spotify have produced accepted foreground state.

nodes.name: RSD tunnel
nodes.detail: The persistent remote developer tunnel carries Apple TV trace data to the collector.
nodes.evidence: The production path is working and no tunnel change is part of phase 1.

nodes.name: Foreground collector
nodes.detail: Publishes retained foreground identity with a bounded brief-ambiguity grace period and full wake/screensaver/outage guards.
nodes.evidence: Collector 36dc7c21 deployed; 31 tests passed, normal switching accepted at about 2 seconds.

nodes.name: Mosquitto
nodes.detail: A dedicated account publishes retained state and availability through authenticated QoS 1 topics.
nodes.evidence: The production MQTT handoff is working.

nodes.name: MQTT config entry
nodes.detail: Home Assistant uses its supported MQTT integration for the local broker.
nodes.evidence: The discovered foreground sensor is loaded and available.

nodes.name: Foreground App sensor
nodes.detail: The sensor exposes the accepted app identity and event metadata to the Denon relay.
nodes.evidence: Netflix reached MQTT at 05:54:45.904 UTC in the latest capture.

nodes.name: Denon App Volume relay
nodes.detail: The relay applies playback ownership and forwards an eligible foreground event to the ESP32.
nodes.evidence: Deployed HEAD 31e5145 with integration hash 8cd5 is healthy; all 51 focused tests pass.

nodes.name: ESP32 app API
nodes.detail: The API accepts an eligible app event once and starts restoration from its stored row.

nodes.name: Per-app volume memory
nodes.detail: NVS keeps each learned app volume and restores the eligible app's value.
nodes.evidence: Home is restored and saved at raw 100, display 50.0. Netflix remains 61.0 and all other seven rows are unchanged.

nodes.name: Target-volume controller
nodes.detail: Restores stored targets with fresh Denon feedback, 750 ms app debounce and a full quiet period before learning after failed restores.
nodes.evidence: Firmware c72b48ec flashed and hash-verified. Home 50 and Netflix 61 accepted in both directions; screensaver retained volume.

nodes.name: ESP32 connectivity
nodes.detail: Wi-Fi and bonded Bluetooth provide the production connection.
nodes.evidence: User accepted operation on the original separate USB adapter. The exact cause of the earlier intermittent outage remains unproven.

nodes.name: Denon Bluetooth SPP
nodes.detail: Bluetooth SPP carries commands and validated receiver feedback while the receiver stays on TV Audio.
nodes.evidence: The latest capture showed the expected feedback progression and no ESP error.

evidence.text: User accepted screensaver behavior and production on the original USB adapter, then requested project closure. Release 0d06c30 is accepted; no more live changes are planned. Earlier timeline entries describe their state at that time.
Refreshed-phone-UI-open switching passed in both directions on firmware c72b48ec. Home to Netflix and Netflix to Home each felt about 2 seconds; exact targets were 61.0 and 50.0.
Live GET confirmed Home raw 100, display and saved value 50.0, connected, idle and error-free. The other seven app rows were unchanged.

Historical checkpoint, superseded by final acceptance: No clear user-observed latency improvement over phase 1 is accepted yet. Screensaver, rapid-transition and original-adapter checks remain pending.

Historical checkpoint, superseded by final acceptance: UART and passive MQTT acceptance capture is active. Faster switching, phone Web UI stability and screensaver behavior remain physically unaccepted.

Flashed firmware c72b48ec application-only at offset 0x10000 and 115200 baud. Esptool verified the data hash. Wi-Fi and Bluetooth reconnected; GET state returned connected, idle and error-free at raw 122, with all eight app rows preserved.

Historical checkpoint, superseded by final acceptance: A phone-WebUI-open Netflix switch completed on unchanged live firmware under Mac USB power and physically reached 61.0. UART logged WiFiClient EAGAIN, but there was no panic, watchdog reset or network loss. The earlier deployed disappearance remains unresolved and intermittent.
A private 4 MB flash backup completed, and the live app image matches the accepted HEAD lineage.
Historical checkpoint, superseded by final acceptance: Home was accidentally learned at 54.0. Restore it to the expected 50.0 through ordinary manual learning after the firmware fix.

Historical checkpoint, superseded by final acceptance: The phone Web UI failure reproduced with normal Home Assistant traffic and no ESP developer polling. Netflix was detected promptly, then the HA backup and app POST timed out; Home Assistant reported no route to host, ARP was incomplete and Mac TCP also timed out. The phone page still showed Connected and 60.0, which may have been cached or stale. Cause remains open.

The phase 1 ambiguity change was exercised live: offline at 06:23:21.096 UTC recovered to Netflix at 21.575, or 0.479 seconds versus the 3.55 second baseline. This trial does not measure movement latency because the ESP32 network failure blocked restoration.

First post-deploy normal switch passed. MQTT reported Netflix at 06:07:30.204 UTC, restoration began at 31.853, first observed movement reached raw 118 at 32.466, exact raw 122 arrived at 34.410 and idle followed at 34.919. There was no error or overshoot.

Historical checkpoint, superseded by final acceptance: Full phase 1 physical acceptance remains open. This trial had no offline or ambiguity event, so it did not exercise the shortened branch; repeat, reverse and screensaver checks are next.
Phase 1 deployed after a verified backup. Live collector SHA 36dc7c21 is active as PID 4173979 with zero restarts; fresh Home state is online and the ESP32 remains stable at 50.0 with no error.

Historical checkpoint, superseded by final acceptance: Phase 2 will first reproduce the reported phone Web UI automation stop. Its cause is not confirmed. Any fix and residual debounce tuning will share one reviewed firmware flash.

The baseline Home 50.0 to Netflix 61.0 transition took 5.60 seconds to first observed movement: 3.55 seconds to MQTT recovery, 1.60 seconds to ESP restoration and 0.46 seconds to motion. Raw feedback reached 122 before idle with no error.
